segments.expected: There were people on every foot of the rail, three deep. The first company had come, all sixteen, because Coombe had said on Monday that anybody who was not standing a floor that day might watch and learn. Behind them there were the reserves, and a dozen juniors who had come down the hill at six with Bettony at their head, and Orla on a crate that somebody had carried down the steps for her, and Healer Aske by the old mast with his bag. segments.expected: On the cinder there was the cart, and the grey ward over the cage.

segments.expected: The yard took her. The cinder took her, and the skin under the cinder, which was cold and hard and did not take a boot. She felt it under her soles as one feels ice on a pond, and she felt it try to rise. It lifted, a finger's breadth, at the far edge, under her weight.

segments.expected: "Me," said Jude. He had come off the string's flank. "And Cade."
segments.transcript: Me, said Jude. He had come off the string's flank. And Cade.

segments.expected: They hauled. The neck came up. The rung came into it off the skin's edge, slowly, as Kiva stood on the far edge with her still door planted and two dead fingers that could tell her nothing about whether she was going to be folded into a sack with sixty drams of ash; and Anwen's wall stood with the string leaning on it; and at the race, by the steps, the lodger lay along the coping and did not lift its tip.

segments.expected: He went. He went along the race on his bad leg, slowly, on the cinder side of the coping, with his kill unlit, and the lodger lay along the stone and did not lift its tip; and when he was above the middle of it he lit, and the kill came down out of his shoulder into the stone of the coping and through the grey cord lying on it.

segments.expected: It did not fall. It came apart. It went to ash all along its length at once, from the cut both ways, as a fuse goes, and lay on the coping in a grey line, a hand high, and then slid off the lip into the dry race, and lay there among the leaves.

segments.expected: She went. Four paces east, low, with the cord riding along her fist, and at the top of the bound, with the struts running out of her calves and the Ember beginning to close, she said it again, short, with the swallow.

segments.expected: "Friday the 13th. The Old Yard. The handed crossing, called; four tries before the Marshal, on the Low Lane's mast, unsanctioned. Finch, two wards, 0.12. Cade, two stances, 0.06. Rowan, Embers, off her own thimble. Spent, 0.18. Held, three and six hundredths." He shut the book. "Sealed, eight-tenths. That adds."

segments.expected: "It's cold. The wax is stiff. That's why you've a little finger." Pru showed her. She did it slowly, as she had done it for Pike by a stove, and the little finger came across the first turn from the far side and held it while the long end went under, and nothing slackened. "There. It's a second pin. You'll not get it today. I didn't get it for a fortnight, and I'd been tying since I was twelve."

segments.expected: The string had come out facing north. It stood with its head toward the lattice and its skin laid down behind it on the south, downhill, toward the race.

segments.expected: "So if we hunt, and somebody's hurt. On our own entry. It's not Sorn's slate. It's not an officer's."
segments.transcript: So if we hunt and somebody's hurt on our own entry, it's not sawn slate, it's not an officus.
